title: How do four subtractions become additions of the inverse?
description: Four subtractions are rewritten as additions of the inverse. The move of a lift shows why taking away a move is the same as adding its inverse. Keeko's doubt is that only the minus sign changes.
teaching_notes: One idea: subtracting a number is the same as adding its inverse, so both the sign of the operation and the number change. Watch for the slip of changing only the minus to plus.

source: Rewrite each subtraction as addition of the inverse: a. (+7) - (+5)  b. (-3) - (+8)  c. (+8) - (-2)  d. (+6) - (-9)
video_script.why: The child rewrites a subtraction as adding the inverse, changing both the operation and the number, and sees why with the moves of a lift.
video_script.substitution: Replace take away by plus, and replace the number by its inverse.
video_script.anchor: the lift of the book, where taking away a move up is the same as a move down
video_script.wrong_answer: I only change the minus to plus
video_script.wrong_move: changes only the minus sign to plus and keeps the second number as it is, so the lift would move the wrong way
video_script.payoff_line: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its inverse.

final_answer.spoken: seven plus negative five, negative three plus negative eight, eight plus positive two, and six plus positive nine

maths_rules: the inverse of +5 is -5; the inverse of -2 is +2
demo: (+9) - (+4) becomes (+9) + (-4), which is 5; taking away a move up 4 equals a move down 4
slip: changing only the minus to plus gives 7 + 5 = 12, but 7 - 5 = 2
video_script.design: A lift with a button panel; the demo shows a move up four taken away and a move down four added. Each subtraction is rewritten with the sign and the number changed together.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the four subtractions (+7) - (+5), (-3) - (+8), (+8) - (-2), (+6) - (-9) in a list

marks.ask: four subtractions slide in as a list

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about subtraction.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Four subtractions are given, and each must be written as an addition.
<bookmark mark='look'/>In the third one, we take away negative two. What do we add instead?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: lift: take away up 4 = down 4;  9 - 4 = 5 and 9 + (-4) = 5;  inverse = opposite sign

marks.lift: a lift with a move up four crossed out and a move down four beside it
marks.demo: 9 - 4 = 5 and 9 + (-4) = 5 are written side by side
marks.inv: +5 and -5 are joined by an arrow and labelled opposite signs

narration: <bookmark mark='lift'/>In a lift, taking away a move up four floors is the same as a move down four.
<bookmark mark='demo'/>Nine take away four is five, and nine plus negative four is five too.
<bookmark mark='inv'/>The number with the opposite sign is the inverse.

marks.given: the four subtractions are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four subtractions.

beats.on_screen: To find: each as an addition of the inverse

marks.find: the words addition of the inverse are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each one as an addition of the inverse.

beats.on_screen: a. (+7) - (+5): take away becomes plus, +5 becomes -5;  b. (-3) - (+8): -8

marks.a: the take away in (+7) - (+5) turns to plus and +5 turns to -5

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, seven take away positive five. Change the take away to plus, and the number to its inverse, negative five.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>That gives seven plus negative five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Negative three take away positive eight becomes negative three plus negative eight.

beats.on_screen: c. (+8) - (-2): take away becomes plus, -2 becomes +2;  d. (+6) - (-9): +9

marks.c: the take away in (+8) - (-2) turns to plus and -2 turns to +2

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step two, eight take away negative two. The inverse of negative two is positive two.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>That gives eight plus positive two.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Six take away negative nine becomes six plus positive nine.

marks.pay: the sentence is written under the additions

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first two are seven plus negative five, and negative three plus negative eight.
The last two are eight plus positive two, and six plus positive nine.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Subtracting a number is the same as adding its inverse.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.fix: 7 - 5 = 2 is written and 12 is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks, I only change the minus to plus, so seven take away five is seven plus five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But seven take away five is two, and seven plus five is twelve.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The number must change to its inverse too, so it is seven plus negative five.
